passages.note: Vote detail page shows Gillette voting Y on House Final Reading of HCR2060, which passed 31-29-0-0-0, but the bill's content is border-crossing and benefits/e-verify enforcement, not deportation of already-present undocumented immigrants.

passages.provision_quote: This section may only be enforced prospectively. This section does not apply retroactively and shall not be construed to apply to the conduct of any person who entered this state unlawfully from a foreign nation at any time before this section becomes enforceable.
passages.note: The bill's illegal-entry crime and foreign-nation return-order apply only prospectively to future border crossers and expressly exclude anyone who entered before the section is enforceable, so the instrument does not speak to deporting undocumented immigrants already in the country.
Bill overview lists Toma as prime sponsor and the vote tallies across stages of HCR2060, confirming the instrument but naming no individual voter and no deportation-scope clause.

rows.reasoning: HCR2060 (2024) creates a new, prospective-only illegal-entry crime with a foreign-nation return order and criminalizes benefits/e-verify fraud, but it "does not apply retroactively and shall not be construed to apply to the conduct of any person who entered this state unlawfully from a foreign nation at any time before this section becomes enforceable," so it does not reach the population this ladder's rungs differ on, those already present as undocumented immigrants, whether "recent arrivals" or "long-settled." Gillette's Y vote on House Final Reading is therefore adjacent to this question, not on it, and no passage here establishes a chair.
